title: Wu-Tang's one-copy album: $2M, seized by the government, resold for $4M
take: They tried to make music priceless by making it impossible to hear. It became a legal mess instead.

caption:
Wu-Tang Clan made exactly one copy of an album, and the story of what happened to it is wilder than any song on it.

It was sold in 2015 for a reported $2 million to Martin Shkreli, the "pharma bro" the internet loved to hate. The U.S. government later seized it. In 2021, a crypto collective called PleasrDAO paid about $4 million. The rules stayed: no commercial release for 88 years.

A new Netflix documentary, The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable, revisits the saga. One critic called the whole thing a "historic blunder" for treating an album like a painting.

Can music be priceless if nobody can hear it?

Source: Rolling Stone, ARTnews
